entries.definition: A benchmark for agents doing real work in a terminal: each task ships an instruction, a containerised Docker sandbox and verifying tests, scoring outcome-based success rather than command-by-command similarity. Created with the Laude Institute, it is run through the Harbor harness (`harbor run -d terminal-bench/...`) and is now a headline number in frontier-model announcements alongside SWE-bench Verified. Terminal-Bench 2.x is the current iteration. In practice: model announcements and internal evals quote "Terminal-Bench 2.x %" as the measure of agentic, end-to-end CLI competence. По-русски: какой у модели процент на Terminal-Bench 2, а не только на SWE-bench? (since May 2025)
entries.clarification: Not only SWE-bench, HumanEval or MBPP as coding benchmarks; terminal agent work has its own outcome-scored benchmark.

entries.definition: A ~2,500-question, multimodal, expert-written closed-ended benchmark spanning 100+ subjects, built by CAIS and Scale AI explicitly as a successor to saturated tests like MMLU. It is now a standard headline number in frontier-model launches. Frontier scores climbed from single digits at launch to roughly half the set by 2026 - the trajectory itself is the point of the benchmark. In practice: model cards and comparison tables quote "HLE %" alongside GPQA and ARC-AGI-2. По-русски: какой у модели процент на Humanity's Last Exam, а не на MMLU? (since January 2025)
entries.clarification: Not MMLU, HellaSwag or BIG-bench as the frontier knowledge benchmark; HLE is the successor number quoted at launches.

entries.definition: The second-generation Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus benchmark and prize, designed after frontier systems began beating the original ARC-AGI-1: grid puzzles calibrated so that every task is solvable by at least two humans in two attempts while remaining very hard for models, with an explicit efficiency/cost dimension. Distinct from ARC-AGI-1 (2019) - quoting "ARC-AGI" without the version is now ambiguous. In practice: labs report "ARC-AGI-2 score at $X per task" to claim novel-problem reasoning rather than recall. По-русски: сравни модели по ARC-AGI-2 с ценой за задачу, а не по старому ARC-AGI (since March 2025)
entries.clarification: Not the original 2019 ARC-AGI with o3's 2024 result; unversioned 'ARC-AGI' is now ambiguous.

entries.term: SWE-bench Pro / the SWE-bench Verified problem
entries.definition: SWE-bench Verified (the human-validated 500-problem subset) became the default agentic-coding metric in 2024-25, but by 2026 practitioners treat it as saturated and contamination-prone. **SWE-bench Pro** is the harder, less-contaminated successor using more difficult repositories with stronger licensing/leakage controls, where frontier scores sit far below Verified's. Terminal-Bench and SWE-Lancer play similar successor roles for CLI and economic-value framing. In practice: engineers now say "Verified is saturated, what's the Pro number?" when reading a model announcement. По-русски: Verified уже сатурирован - какой у модели результат на SWE-bench Pro? (since 2025)
entries.clarification: Do not treat SWE-bench Verified percentages as the definitive uncontaminated measure of coding ability; it is saturated.

entries.definition: METR's metric for agent capability: the length of task - measured as how long a human expert takes - that a model can complete with 50% success probability. Their March 2025 paper found this horizon doubling roughly every 7 months from 2019 to early 2025; later revisions with a harder task suite suggest faster doubling. It reframes progress as "how long a job can it finish unattended" rather than as a benchmark percentage. In practice: leaders say "the time horizon is now a few hours" to argue about which workflows can be delegated to agents. По-русски: по METR временной горизонт агентов уже часы - что можно делегировать? (since March 2025)
entries.clarification: Do not answer with benchmark accuracy percentages; this metric is human task duration completed at 50% success.
